bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Volatility in crude/PVC prices; Geopolitical tensions impacting freight/logistics (Middle East/Europe); Labor code cost inflation; Customer concentration in auto OEMs; FX reversal risk.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on structural margin re-rating (25-30% vs historical 24-25%); Conservative on guiding specific quarterly numbers but firm on annual growth trajectories; Transparent on FX and labor code impacts.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The margin jump to 31% is not just cyclical but structural due to the mix shift to auto exports (50% growth) which are dollar-priced and higher margin. The INR 3 Cr Q4 FX gain is small relative to the operational leverage gained from the export mix. Employee cost spike is a one-time regulatory adjustment (new labor codes) rather than aggressive hiring.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Largest capacity for manufacturing of synthetic leather in the domestic organised segment
- Product breadth - more than 400 variants of artificial leather from PVC polymer, spanning interior trim applications meeting worldwide standards
- Diversified clientele across automotive (BMW, Mercedes Benz, Chrysler, Ford, Hyundai, MG, KIA, Maruti Suzuki, Tata, Toyota, Mahindra & Mahindra, ISUZU, Suzuki, Honda, Renualt, Skoda/Volkswagen, Stellantis, Hero, Bajaj, Royal Enfield, TVS, Piaggio, Sonalika Tractor, Lear, TS Tech Sun, Bharat Seat, Krishna Maruti, Sharda Motors, S.I. Interpact Group, Swaraj Auto, Polor Auto) and footwear (Bata, Paragon, Lancer, Action, Relaxo, VKC Group)
- In-house R&D with prototype laboratories that deliver a good number of samples on every working day, developing new textures, colours, patterns and functionalities
- Global delivery footprint through wholly owned subsidiaries - Mayur Uniquoters Corp. (Texas, USA), Mayur Uniquoters SA (Pty) Ltd (South Africa), Mayur Tecfab Private Limited (Jaipur, Rajasthan) - and step-down subsidiaries Futura Textiles Inc. (Nevada, USA) and UAB Futura Textiles Europe (Lithuania)
- Just-in-time supply of artificial leather to OEM customers in the USA through Mayur Uniquoters Corp., which carries no manufacturing beyond customer-driven job work
- Exports to automotive OEMs Mercedes Benz and BMW in the South African market, facilitated by the subsidiary Mayur Uniquoters SA (Pty) Ltd
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material availability and supply reliability — Management lists as threats that some raw material is not available locally, increasing cost and affecting competitiveness, and that supply of raw material is irregular; increases in raw material prices are also named among the risks and concerns the Company continuously monitors.
- Foreign exchange exposure — Unfavourable foreign exchange rate fluctuation is listed as a threat and foreign exchange fluctuation is named among the risks and concerns the Company continuously monitors - material for a business whose overseas subsidiaries drove a significant part of the year's sales increase.
- Single-segment, single-product concentration — The Company deals only in one segment - manufacturing and sale of PU/PVC synthetic leather - and reports a single reportable segment, so there is no internal diversification to absorb a demand or pricing shock in artificial leather.
- Geographical concentration — Geographical concentration is explicitly named in the MD&A Risks and Concerns list among the risks the Company monitors, alongside macro-economic factors.
- Rising competition and logistics cost — Increase in competition is listed as a threat, as is increase in logistics cost; both bear directly on realisations and on landed cost competitiveness in a business whose material competes on being a cheaper alternative to natural leather.
- Product sustainability - non-biodegradability and the innovation race — Non-biodegradability of synthetic leather is listed as a threat. The BRSR materiality table adds that failure to innovate and adapt to changing sustainability trends may reduce market competitiveness and customer preference, that increasing regulatory requirements on product sustainability and chemicals may create compliance risks, and that inability to meet customer expectations for sustainable products may cost business opportunities - relevant given the market's shift to water-based PU, solvent-free coatings and bio-based feedstocks.
- Climate, emissions and energy transition risk — The Company flags that customer and regulatory expectations may increase compliance and operational costs, that failure to reduce emissions may result in reputational risks, reduced market access and loss of business opportunities, and that physical climate risks such as extreme weather events may disrupt operations and supply chains. On energy it flags that rising energy prices and dependence on conventional energy sources may increase operating costs and transition risks, that energy supply disruptions can affect production continuity and operational efficiency, and that increasing regulatory requirements related to energy efficiency and climate change may result in additional compliance obligations.
- Water and waste - operational continuity and compliance — Water scarcity, declining groundwater levels and climate change may impact water availability for operations; increasing water costs and regulatory requirements may increase operational expenses; inefficient water use or inadequate wastewater management may result in environmental impacts, compliance risks and reputational damage; and water-related disruptions may affect production continuity. On waste, improper handling, storage or disposal may result in environmental pollution, regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
- Policy and regulatory change — Changes in government policy and legislation are named among the risks the Company monitors, and management separately lists lack of poor policies for the specific development of the sector as a threat. Risks are overseen under a Risk Management Policy reviewed by the Audit and Risk Management Committee, with insurance policies taken to mitigate other risks.

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells PU/PVC synthetic leather and operates a single reportable segment. Its material finds application in footwear (shoes/sandals insole and uppers), automotive (seat upholstery and inner linings), furniture and fashion items (apparel) and leather goods, and it states it has the largest capacity for manufacturing of synthetic leather in the domestic organised segment, with annual production capacity of 48.60 Million linear meters of PVC coated fabric and 5.00 Million Linear meter of PU coated fabric. Overseas supply and trading are routed through wholly owned and step-down subsidiaries, and a retail furnishing business is run under the brand TEXTURE AND HUES through the wholly owned subsidiary Mayur Tecfab Private Limited.

outlook.body: No fixed order book; business runs on monthly volume projections from OEMs. Export auto OEM revenue for FY26 was INR 290 Cr vs INR 194 Cr in FY25 (+50%).

outlook.body: Expansion of Ford platforms; penetration in European/US marine and furnishing segments; potential greenfield global plant (INR 300 Cr) to bypass tariffs/logistics.

outlook.body:
- Vision to be the preferred supplier of automotive, footwear and leather goods material to leading OEMs in the world
- Continued focus on efficiency and productivity for future readiness, with cautious optimism
- Development of new types of high-quality PU coated fabric and broader product diversification
- Optimising production cost, backed by effective cost savings plans and modernised manufacturing units
- Expanding exports to neighbouring and Western markets, positioning India as an export hub for artificial leather into Europe and North America
- Strengthening the international footprint through wholly owned and step-down subsidiaries covering the USA, South Africa and Lithuania, which management calls a milestone in Mayur's journey into the African and USA markets
- Serving retail customers through the TEXTURE AND HUES retail furnishing brand run via the wholly owned subsidiary Mayur Tecfab Private Limited
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The bundle carries no named plant, line or capacity-addition project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. What the Company does state is its existing scale: it has the largest capacity for manufacturing of synthetic leather in the domestic organised segment, with annual production capacity of 48.60 Million linear meters of PVC coated fabric and 5.00 Million Linear meter of PU coated fabric, and it manufactures more than 400 variants of artificial leather from PVC polymer. Expansion intent appears only as funding language in the dividend section - profit is retained to maintain healthy financial leverage 'with a view to support and fund the future expansion plans' - and as continued focus on efficiency and productivity. The only physical build-out actually described is environmental and CSR infrastructure: solar power installations and adoption of renewable energy under the Net Zero roadmap (the Company states it is committed to net zero by 2050), rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge projects, more than 47000 large-scale tree plantation, plus educational infrastructure such as classrooms, sanitation facilities and libraries. On the rupee quantum: a 'Capital commitments' note (note 37, capital expenditure contracted for at the end of the reporting year but not recognised as liabilities) does exist in the accounts, but the figure arrives with no unit printed in the block and is therefore unusable; the note states only that the amount is net of a capital advance of Rs.75.65 lakhs (March 2025: Rs.19.84 lakhs).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global synthetic leather market estimated at USD 49.10 billion in 2025 and projected to reach around USD 103.91 billion by 2035, a CAGR of approximately 7.78 percent between 2026 and 2035
- Asia Pacific synthetic leather market estimated at USD 21.07 billion in 2025 and projected to reach around USD 45.93 billion by 2035 at a CAGR of approximately 8.1 percent, with India, China and South Korea the principal growth drivers; Asia Pacific holds over 43 percent of global value
- Automotive is expected to be the fastest-growing application at a 13.2% CAGR, supported by rapid expansion of electric vehicles and premium interior customization programs
- Footwear remains the largest application by revenue share at over 31 percent, with rising footwear production in China, India, Vietnam and Indonesia driving substitution into synthetic material
- PU synthetic leather holds the largest product share at over 53 percent, with innovation concentrated in water-based PU systems, solvent-free coatings, microfiber structures and bio-based feedstocks
- Rising demand for animal-free and sustainable products is a major driver, with synthetic leather positioned as a cheaper alternative to natural leather with good aesthetic quality
- Low-VOC and odour-controlled materials meeting strict cabin air quality standards are being pulled by automotive and premium footwear customers
- Profit after tax improved on effective cost savings plans, increase in sales price and a significant increase in sales in overseas subsidiaries, with management stating the subsidiaries contributed significantly to consolidated revenue
- Headwinds management flags: unfavourable foreign exchange rate fluctuations, some raw material not available locally which increases cost and affects competitiveness, and irregular supply of raw material
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Mayur Uniquoters delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with PAT up 73% YoY (standalone), driven by a structural shift toward high-margin automotive exports (up 50% YoY) and favorable FX realization. Management guides for sustained 25-30% EBITDA margins and ~15-20% export growth, underpinned by a low-capex capacity addition (INR 50 Cr) commissioning by year-end.

open.item: Buyback not yet decided/discussed; typically considered after final (year-end) results.
Guidance to maintain 25-26% margin, with potential 25-30% in long term given export mix and currency; not committing to sustained 30%.
Price hike taken for domestic footwear/open market in Q4; automotive price increase (from March RM rise) to reflect in Q1FY27, both RM cost and price impacts.
Ordered a coating line to be installed in existing facility (not South India), capex within ~INR50 crores, to be done by end of calendar year 2026.
Domestic value growth guidance of 8-10% for FY27 and next 2-3 years.
Export value growth guidance of 15-20% (up to 25%) for FY27 and coming years, automotive-led.
Export mix expected around 40-45% of revenue in FY27 (from 42.5% in FY26).
Global-location plant (Mexico or other country) capex ~INR300 crores still under evaluation; location not finalized.
New coating line to add ~5 lakh meters/month (4-6 range), increasing revenue by ~INR120-150 crores.
Targeting growth in general export (marine, furnishing) and new segments in Europe/USA beyond automotive; currency depreciation gives competitiveness.
EU-India FTA (zero duty, ~10-12 months to sign) expected to strongly help non-automotive/general export business; US remains first target market.

verdicts.item: 10% US tariff on India from April 2025 flagged; management states their material is not under US customs duty tariff category, no tariff impact currently.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'when the US tariff came, our general export business did not go down... the impact of the US duty is not visible in the overall year' — OEM unaffected, but the expected general-export uplift wa…

verdicts.item: Export OEM growth expected at least 15% this year and 15-20% next year, growing at least 15% for the next 3 years.
verdicts.note: Vinod: 'Auto exports for the current year INR290 Cr., and last year it was INR194 Cr... increased by about 50%'; Arun: 'our export growth is 35%.'

verdicts.item: Management planning to professionalize the organization; process ongoing.
verdicts.note: Q4FY26 call run by ED Mr. Arun Bagaria and the CFO (Chairman/MD Poddar not on the management panel) — professionalization progressing.

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of ~10-15% (12-15%) top-line growth.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we registered a total growth of 15% in value.'

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 15-20% bottom-line growth.
verdicts.note: Standalone Q4 PBT +70%, PAT +73% YoY with ~30% margins — FY26 bottom-line growth exceeded 15-20%. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Mexico plant postponed due to tariff confusion but intact; will proceed once tariff situation settles, not considering other location.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'it could be Mexico or some other country'; and instead of a fresh South India plant, 'we have found space in an existing facility' — contradicts 'not considering other location.'

verdicts.item: Auto OEM export unaffected by US tariff (Tier-1 supply via Mexico); no worry up to 25% tariff, but newly announced 50% tariff (from 27 Aug) on select items is a worry, needs analysis.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'our general export business did not go down... the impact of the US duty is not visible in the overall year' — auto OEM unaffected; general export uplift nullified by the duty.

verdicts.item: Working 6-8 months with big brands (Aditya Birla, Adidas) on footwear/leather goods/garments; trial orders started, full ramp expected in 1-2 years with better margins.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we are definitely talking to a lot of brands. But business has not matured till now... approved us as a vendor. But no price commercial settlement has happened till now.'

verdicts.item: Won order from Ford for super models; supply to grow from ~10,000 yards to more than 100,000 yards in the next 2 years.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'our volume with Ford was very low. So, we have added more platforms on Ford business. The business has started increasing. But it will increase more in the coming months.'

verdicts.item: In discussions with Ford Motor in South Africa; discussion already started to add customers.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we have added more platforms on Ford business. The business has started increasing' — Ford customer expanding (US market).

verdicts.item: Replacement market stagnant (3-4 OEMs down, design changes); no massive increase expected but slight improvement.
verdicts.note: Q4 breakup: 'Replacement INR41 crores' vs Q3 INR38.84 cr — continued slight improvement.

verdicts.item: Strategy to diversify across segments (automotive, footwear, leather goods, garments) and never depend on one customer; working with US Stellantis and expanding models.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we are trying to enter into new segments also... growth in the marine... furnishing... other markets also in Europe and in the USA. So, we are working on all angles' — diversification ongoing, …

risks.risk: Raw material availability and supply reliability
risks.note: Management lists as threats that some raw material is not available locally, increasing cost and affecting competitiveness, and that supply of raw material is irregular; increases in raw material prices are also named among the risks and concerns the Company continuously monitors.

Unfavourable foreign exchange rate fluctuation is listed as a threat and foreign exchange fluctuation is named among the risks and concerns the Company continuously monitors - material for a business whose overseas subsidiaries drove a significant part of the year's sales increase.

The Company deals only in one segment - manufacturing and sale of PU/PVC synthetic leather - and reports a single reportable segment, so there is no internal diversification to absorb a demand or pricing shock in artificial leather.
Geographical concentration is explicitly named in the MD&A Risks and Concerns list among the risks the Company monitors, alongside macro-economic factors.

Increase in competition is listed as a threat, as is increase in logistics cost; both bear directly on realisations and on landed cost competitiveness in a business whose material competes on being a cheaper alternative to natural leather.

risks.risk: Product sustainability - non-biodegradability and the innovation race
risks.note: Non-biodegradability of synthetic leather is listed as a threat. The BRSR materiality table adds that failure to innovate and adapt to changing sustainability trends may reduce market competitiveness and customer preference, that increasing regulatory requirements on product sustainability and chemicals may create compliance risks, and that inability to meet customer expectations for sustainable products may cost business opportunities - relevant given the market's shift to water-based PU, solvent-free coatings and bio-based feedstocks.

risks.risk: Climate, emissions and energy transition risk
risks.note: The Company flags that customer and regulatory expectations may increase compliance and operational costs, that failure to reduce emissions may result in reputational risks, reduced market access and loss of business opportunities, and that physical climate risks such as extreme weather events may disrupt operations and supply chains. On energy it flags that rising energy prices and dependence on conventional energy sources may increase operating costs and transition risks, that energy supply disruptions can affect production continuity and operational efficiency, and that increasing regulatory requirements related to energy efficiency and climate change may result in additional compliance obligations.

risks.risk: Water and waste - operational continuity and compliance
risks.note: Water scarcity, declining groundwater levels and climate change may impact water availability for operations; increasing water costs and regulatory requirements may increase operational expenses; inefficient water use or inadequate wastewater management may result in environmental impacts, compliance risks and reputational damage; and water-related disruptions may affect production continuity. On waste, improper handling, storage or disposal may result in environmental pollution, regulatory penalties and reputational damage.

Changes in government policy and legislation are named among the risks the Company monitors, and management separately lists lack of poor policies for the specific development of the sector as a threat. Risks are overseen under a Risk Management Policy reviewed by the Audit and Risk Management Committee, with insurance policies taken to mitigate other risks.

one-line thesis: Mayur Uniquoters delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with PAT up 73% YoY (standalone), driven by a structural shift toward high-margin automotive exports (up 50% YoY) and favorable FX realization. Management guides for sustained 25-30% EBITDA margins and ~15-20% export growth, underpinned by a low-capex capacity addition (INR 50 Cr) commissioning by year-end.

growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of Ford platforms; penetration in European/US marine and furnishing segments; potential greenfield global plant (INR 300 Cr) to bypass tariffs/logistics.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells PU/PVC synthetic leather and operates a single reportable segment. Its material finds application in footwear (shoes/sandals insole and uppers), automotive (seat upholstery and inner linings), furniture and fashion items (apparel) and leather goods, and it states it has the largest capacity for manufacturing of synthetic leather in the domestic organised segment, with annual production capacity of 48.60 Million linear meters of PVC coated fabric and 5.00 Million Linear meter of PU coated fabric. Overseas supply and trading are routed through wholly owned and step-down subsidiaries, and a retail furnishing business is run under the brand TEXTURE AND HUES through the wholly owned subsidiary Mayur Tecfab Private Limited.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global synthetic leather market estimated at USD 49.10 billion in 2025 and projected to reach around USD 103.91 billion by 2035, a CAGR of approximately 7.78 percent between 2026 and 2035
- Asia Pacific synthetic leather market estimated at USD 21.07 billion in 2025 and projected to reach around USD 45.93 billion by 2035 at a CAGR of approximately 8.1 percent, with India, China and South Korea the principal growth drivers; Asia Pacific holds over 43 percent of global value
- Automotive is expected to be the fastest-growing application at a 13.2% CAGR, supported by rapid expansion of electric vehicles and premium interior customization programs
- Footwear remains the largest application by revenue share at over 31 percent, with rising footwear production in China, India, Vietnam and Indonesia driving substitution into synthetic material
- PU synthetic leather holds the largest product share at over 53 percent, with innovation concentrated in water-based PU systems, solvent-free coatings, microfiber structures and bio-based feedstocks
- Rising demand for animal-free and sustainable products is a major driver, with synthetic leather positioned as a cheaper alternative to natural leather with good aesthetic quality
- Low-VOC and odour-controlled materials meeting strict cabin air quality standards are being pulled by automotive and premium footwear customers
- Profit after tax improved on effective cost savings plans, increase in sales price and a significant increase in sales in overseas subsidiaries, with management stating the subsidiaries contributed significantly to consolidated revenue
- Headwinds management flags: unfavourable foreign exchange rate fluctuations, some raw material not available locally which increases cost and affects competitiveness, and irregular supply of raw material

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

Management guides for sustained 25-30% EBITDA margins and ~15-20% export growth, underpinned by a low-capex capacity addition (INR 50 Cr) commissioning by year-end.
